angle: Sisay's real currency is access — every colour on a fair legendary body widens what she can fetch (3, 10, 23, 28, 33) — and the issue's proof piece is a checker holding that cut 'two-card infinite' down to something more useful: a real, unbounded, zero-life combat loop with the mana base as its third member.

departments.headline: COUNT COLOURS, NOT CARDS
departments.dek: Why do good Sisay pilots pass with all five pips available and no activation? Because the number that decides what she can find isn't printed on her card — it's the count of distinct colours sitting beside her.

callouts.title: LAND HER, THEN WAIT
callouts.text: She costs {2}{W} and lands on turn three in 8,028 of 10,000 seeded games. On arrival she is a 2/2 with a 'mana value less than 2' gate — three legal fetches in the whole deck. Casting her was never the assignment.

callouts.title: BUY RUNGS ON FAIR BODIES
callouts.text: Every colour among your OTHER legendary permanents is +1/+1 on her and a wider gate. Katilda, Kinnan, Lotho, Saffi, Kambal and Kutzil buy two rungs each for two or three mana. Derevi buys three on one card.

callouts.title: THE 2-TO-3 STEP IS THE GAME
callouts.text: The ladder runs 3, 10, 23, 28, 33 legal targets at power 2 through 6. Two colours to three adds thirteen targets — the biggest jump on the ladder, and the moment a pile of small legends becomes a toolbox.

callouts.title: STOP CLIMBING AT FOUR
callouts.text: Nothing in the deck costs more than five, so four colours already unlocks all 33 targets. The fifth colour buys combat stats and Jodah's anthem — and zero new access. Don't pay for it.

callouts.title: COUNT THE BILL IN PIPS
callouts.text: {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, zero generic. Six cards can carry most of it alone: Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika, Relic of Legends, Selvala. The goldfish lands Sisay beside one 55.8% of the time by turn six. Count coloured sources, never total mana.

pilot_tips.text: Cast it, love it, and never count it toward an activation — {C}{C} pays zero of Sisay's five pips.

captions.Sisay, Weatherlight Captain: **THE SCOREBOARD:** +1/+1 for each colour among your other legendary permanents, and a gate of 'mana value less than her power.' Her stat line is a live count of how much of your library is legal.
captions.Derevi, Empyrial Tactician: **THREE RUNGS, ONE CARD:** white, blue and green at mana value 3. She alone takes Sisay from a 2/2 to a 5/5 and the fetch pool from 3 targets to 28.

departments.pull_quote: Your grace period expires at the third colour. Spend it there.

departments.headline: MULLIGAN FOR ENABLERS
departments.dek: Which seven do you keep in a deck whose payoffs fetch themselves? The Coach wants fuel and a cheap legend; Ledger's ten thousand hands say you keep 84.2% of first sevens — so the judgement is all colour and fuel.

hands.why: Two rungs on fair bodies, the best battery piece in the deck, unrestricted colour. Sisay arrives on curve and the ladder hits three colours by turn five — this is the enabler hand the whole section is asking for.
Five payoffs, two lands, no fixing. Every legend here is a fetch target — this hand holds cards Sisay could have found, and none of the fuel she can't.

The trap keep. It curves out fast and pays nothing: Sol Ring is colourless, the Halfling's mana is legendary-spells-only, the Territory is creature-spells-only. Sisay lands early and stares at a five-pip bill this hand cannot cover.
Three lands with real colour, a rock that pays any pip, a two-rung legend, and interaction to hold. Not flashy — exactly the hand the 84.2% keep rate is made of.

pilot_tips.text: Treat one untapped Bird as the difference between keep and ship — an early accelerant shows up by turn six in only 63.8% of games, so a hand that has one is ahead of the deck's own curve.

captions.Delighted Halfling: **THE FALSE FRIEND:** it ramps Sisay out a turn early and makes her uncounterable — then never pays a single pip of what she does next. A cast-turn card, not an activation-turn card.

departments.headline: COMMIT BEFORE YOU PEEK
departments.dek: Two real boards from this deck's midgame: a Dimir seat holding four cards, and a pod that just watched your first fetch resolve. Pick your line at each fork — the Coach's call is printed after the branches, never before.

pilot_tips.text: Hold it for the activation you intend to convert, not the first one you can afford — one white mana buys the whole turn.

departments.pull_quote: Every activation is public. The decision behind it doesn't have to be.

departments.headline: THE FOURTH-MOST-INTERESTING BOARD
departments.dek: When does a five-colour tutor deck get left alone? Right up until the table can count five untapped colour sources — so your midgame is a game about what the pod can see, and what it can't.

callouts.title: THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: You flip to archenemy when three things land together: three-plus colours among your other legends, five pips visibly payable, and protection up. That is also your pivot — if you're going to wear the label, cash it for the window, not the applause.

callouts.title: THE TELLS, RANKED
callouts.text: An omni-mana body resolving — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika — is louder than any legend you fetch. Najeela is louder still. A second activation in one turn cycle ends the conversation.

pilot_tips.text: Tap Loran while an opponent is deciding whether to attack you — the cheapest goodwill this deck buys is one shared card.

captions.Rhystic Study: **THE DRAWN TRAP:** a Game Changer Sisay can never fetch — and the card most likely to make you archenemy before you've decided to be. Time its arrival like a threat, because the table will.
captions.Shalai, Voice of Plenty: **THE RETIREMENT PLAN:** hexproof for you and every other creature you control. One fetch ends the kill-the-rung attack — get her before you need her, not after.

departments.pull_quote: Play the whole midgame as a fair legends deck — you're never more than one activation from the truth.

departments.headline: FOUR WAYS YOU LOSE
departments.dek: Every pod has a seat that beats you — a wrath, a lock, a swarm, a stack. Know which one you're facing and which of your outs is real before the ladder decides for you.

threats.read: They let you build, then take the board and the ladder in one card — a wrath drops you from 28 legal fetches back to 3. Commit exactly what wins and bank a colour-diverse legend in hand: the hand copy rebuilds two rungs, a board copy dies with the rest.

A five-pip, zero-generic activation has nothing generic to pay around — cost-raisers and land-tappers hit your engine harder than anyone else's. You are the beatdown here: race the lock's completion, and name the piece that breaks the lock on you, not the scariest one.

You can't race roughly 120 life across three seats — and you don't have to. Fetch the taxes instead of casting removal: their creatures arrive tapped, their draws cost life, and your board slides down the target list.

The endgame is a count of held interaction — and yours cannot be fetched: all six counterspells are non-legendary. Hold mana up instead of climbing, and spend Path to Exile the moment the piece lands. It only gets worse from there.

pilot_tips.text: You choose the wipe's timing, so choose the turn you rebuild cheapest — the ladder recovers faster than any board it takes down.

departments.headline: SIX WISHES PER CAPTAIN
departments.dek: Most decks get one wish per tutor card; yours reloads every time you can raise five pips. Here are the six fetches that cover the whole game — and the 26 cards she will never see, so you stop wishing for them.

pilot_tips.text: Know your second choice before you announce — the power check happens on resolution, so the fetch you name is not always the fetch you get.

captions.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: **THE FUEL SHE CAN FIND:** most of the pip battery is invisible to Sisay. Selvala is the piece she can fetch — and with Sisay at power 5, one tap is the whole {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}.

departments.pull_quote: Fetch what only she can reach. Draw the rest.

departments.headline: THE FIVE-COLOUR TECHNICALITY
departments.dek: How does a {2}{W} commander give you a five-colour deck? Because colour identity reads every mana symbol on the card — and Sisay's activation carries all five. The Counselor takes it from the top.
departments.body:
Begin with the zone itself. CR 903.4 sets a commander's colour identity from every mana symbol in its mana cost and rules text — and Sisay's activation, {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, puts all five colours in hers. A {2}{W} card is your licence to sleeve ninety-nine cards in five colours. That is not a loophole; it is the rule working exactly as written, and it is the entire reason this deck exists.

The zone guarantee is worth more here than in most decks. CR 903.8: the command zone gives you guaranteed access at a rising price — {2} more for each previous cast from the zone. Sisay runs 3, then 5, then 7, then 9. Note what the ladder beside this column does not tax: her power is recomputed from the battlefield, so a recast Sisay returns to a surviving board at full strength. Spot removal costs you the tax and a turn. A sweeper costs you the tax and the ladder. Those are different injuries; insure against the second.

The 21-damage clock — CR 903.10a — is on the record but rarely the plan. At four colours she is a 6/6, and three connections is a kill in theory. In practice her power is a gate, not a weapon: the deck's lethal output is the section titled The Kill. Treat commander damage as a bonus the scoreboard occasionally pays out.

Now the Coach's half: protect, don't budget for recasts. The goldfish holds a protection effect by turn six in 79.8% of games — Shalai, Flowering of the White Tree, Plaza of Heroes, and two free instants. A recast costs more than mana; it costs an activation window at a table that has now seen the engine. And the political read is fixed from the pregame: a five-colour commander who tutors on activation is announced as bracket 4 before your first land drop. Don't fight the label — schedule it.

captions.Sisay, Weatherlight Captain: **GUARANTEED ACCESS:** the one card you always have is the one that fetches the rest. The 99 is built so that what she finds matters more than what you draw.

pilot_tips.text: Spend Plaza's last job on the turn that matters: {3}, tap, exile it, and Sisay is hexproof and indestructible through the wrath you can see coming.

departments.pull_quote: A {2}{W} card, a five-colour licence — the rule working exactly as written.

departments.headline: EVERY LEGEND EARNS ITS SEAT
departments.dek: Fifty-nine spells, one question each: does it climb the ladder, pay the bill, or hold the window open? The roster is ranked by load — the six cards that can pay her lead, and the lands report to Sources Say.

cards: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge

The ladder — colours on fair bodies
cards: Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolarian Obliterator

captions.Bloom Tender: **THE BEST CARD SHE CAN'T FIND:** one mana of each colour among permanents you control, compounding with the same colours the ladder counts — and non-legendary, so it must be drawn.
captions.Loran of the Third Path: **THE EXCEPTION:** the deck's one artifact-and-enchantment answer on a legendary body — the only answer Sisay can go and get.

pilot_tips.text: Don't build a cold-start plan on fetching Mikaeus — {X}{W} fetched rather than cast may mean X is 0, and that question is still open on the record.

departments.note: Lands deliberately fall to the Depth group; the mana base gets its own audit in Sources Say. Roster groups feed the Featured Artist overlap table — keep group names short.

departments.headline: CAN THE ENGINE FIND IT?
departments.dek: No sideboard means no bench — all ten names are scouted from the pool, and each was screened the way this deck spends: against a five-pip bill and a tutor that only sees legends. Seven pass outright, led by Gaea's Cradle — a fetch that is live even for a cold-start Sisay.
departments.pull_quote: The bracket floor reads 4 before and 4 after on all ten — none of these is a power-level decision in disguise.
departments.note: The renderer draws the ten from considering.json. Every combo line an entry opens is flagged 'needs a stack scenario' there; keep them priced as candidates.

departments.headline: FIVE PIPS, ZERO GENERIC
departments.dek: Can thirty-nine lands pay a bill with no generic in it? Flat sources against unflat pips is the whole story — this base is priced for the activation, not the cast costs, and the audit zeroes every restricted source before it counts a thing.

pilot_tips.text: Name Human — 'or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type' is the clause that lets this land pay Sisay's activation, which Unclaimed Territory's text never will.

captions.Plaza of Heroes: **READ THE CLAUSE, NOT THE PHRASE:** the legendary-spell mode can't pay an activation, but the third mode — any colour among legendary permanents you control — pays her fine. One land, three different rules.

departments.headline: SHE WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded hands put Sisay on the battlefield by turn three in four games of five — so why does the deck feel slow? Because the real curve is the assembly: commander plus a five-colour source lands by turn six just 55.8% of the time.

callouts.title: TURN THREE, LIKE CLOCKWORK
callouts.text: Mean cast turn 2.96, median 3, 99.1% by turn six — 8,028 of 10,000 games cast her exactly on turn three. Casting the commander is the one promise this deck always keeps.

callouts.title: THE ASSEMBLY IS THE CURVE
callouts.text: Sisay plus a five-colour mana source: mean turn 4.22, 55.8% by turn six. The gap between 'commander out' and 'engine online' is where your mulligans and your first two fetches live.

callouts.title: MANA CROSSES FIVE AT TURN SIX
callouts.text: Mean available mana is 4.06 on turn four and 5.87 on turn six — the five-pip activation is barely affordable on curve even before colours. This is why a battery body is not optional.

departments.pull_quote: The commander arrives on schedule in every simulation. The engine is the thing you build.

departments.headline: PARTIALLY ACCURATE, WHOLLY LETHAL
departments.dek: The combo database pleads Najeela plus Derevi as a two-card infinite. Twenty-four steps and three review cycles later, the record says something better: a real, unbounded, self-funding combat loop that kills the table for zero life — once you can raise the first five pips.

callouts.title: PRE-FUND COMBAT ONE
callouts.text: Three attackers connect and three Derevi triggers come back — two short of the five-pip bill. The first activation is paid by the lands you kept untapped before combat. Budget for it.

callouts.title: BREAK EVEN ON COMBAT TWO
callouts.text: Five creatures connect, five triggers, five pips — the loop funds itself exactly. From here every activation is paid inside the damage step: tap, pass, let a trigger untap the land, tap it again.

callouts.title: RUN AWAY ON COMBAT THREE
callouts.text: Attackers follow 2A−1: three, five, nine, seventeen, thirty-three. Triggers match attackers while the cost stays five. The first defending player leaves during combat 4's damage — as a state-based action, before anyone gets priority.

callouts.title: THE ARMY STAYS
callouts.text: A defending player leaving the game is not on CR 506.4's removal list, so all seventeen attackers remain in combat. Redirect at the next seat — the Commander default makes every opponent a defending player — and combat six ends the game.

callouts.title: THE FLOOR IS ZERO LIFE
callouts.text: Command Tower covers {B} off Sisay's five-colour identity; Plaza of Heroes' third mode covers the rest off Najeela and Derevi's own colours. City of Brass and Mana Confluence never need to be tapped — activating a mana ability is never mandatory.

captions.Najeela, the Blade-Blossom: **THE LOUD HALF:** every Warrior that attacks makes another Warrior, and her five-pip untap shares Sisay's exact cost — the pip battery double-duties as combo fuel.
captions.Derevi, Empyrial Tactician: **THE QUIET HALF:** one untap trigger per creature connecting. Reads as a fair 2/3 right up until the triggers equal the bill.

pilot_tips.text: Fetch her on the turn she wins, not the turn she impresses — until then she is safer in your library than in your hand.

departments.pull_quote: Not a two-card infinite — a two-card engine with the mana base as its third member.

departments.headline: READ TWICE, STAMPED ONCE
departments.dek: One case carries this issue: A-002, the Najeela–Derevi loop — twenty-four steps, every Comprehensive Rules citation quoted verbatim, re-audited across three review passes. The holding, 'partially accurate,' is precisely why you can trust the rest of this magazine.
departments.note: Stacks 001 and 003 carry failing checker verdicts and must not render; their open questions are listed under gaps.

departments.headline: EIGHTY-ONE HANDS
departments.dek: Who painted a deck that refuses to repeat itself? Eighty-one artists across ninety-nine cards, and the leader holds exactly five — a gallery of one-ofs, which is the most singleton fact about a singleton deck.

featured.note:
Five cards of ninety-nine is what leading this roster looks like — nobody else painted more than four, and no product drop or block purchase concentrated anyone's hand. The counting is per card, never per copy.

Belledin's five are quietly load-bearing: two of the three cards a cold-start Sisay can legally fetch (Mox Amber and Mikaeus, the Lunarch), the deck's only fetchable artifact-and-enchantment answer (Loran of the Third Path), Exotic Orchard, and a Forest. The spread is the story — this deck was assembled one card at a time, and the credits prove it.

also_worth_noting.note: Four entries, all lands — Hallowed Fountain, Overgrown Tomb, Steam Vents, Temple Garden. The audit's shock-dual backbone, one hand.
Jegantha, the Wellspring and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse — the battery's one-card payment and the tax shell's heaviest hitter.
Flooded Strand and Windswept Heath — two of the nine fetches.
Esper Sentinel and Grand Abolisher — the white hatebears, both non-legendary, both drawn.
Drannith Magistrate and Kenrith, the Returned King — a Game Changer and a five-colour king.

captions.Loran of the Third Path: **THE BELLEDIN PICK:** if one of his five cards decides a game, it's this one — the only answer in the deck Sisay can fetch.

departments.pull_quote: No drop, no block buy, no house style — ninety-nine cards chosen one at a time, and the credits show it.

rhythm_notes: Canonical five-act order throughout; The Kill is the late peak. The one legal dense adjacency — Sources Say into By the Numbers — is split by the declared full-bleed art break (issue_spec.BREATHER_AFTER), and Sources Say carries no pull quote so the break does the breathing. What's Your Play (participation) is buffered by Keep or Ship practice before and Table Manners reflection after. Judge's Desk sits between The Kill's narrative and Featured Artist's appreciation, closing gently to the Back Page. Pull quotes ride The Game Plan, Table Manners, Fetch Quests, Command Zone, By the Numbers, The Kill and Featured Artist as micro-breathers; Keep or Ship and Know Your Enemy run deliberately lean.
gaps: Stacks 001 and 003 carry checker verdict 'fail'. Between them sits the deck's single highest-leverage open question — can a freshly fetched legend help pay for a second activation in the same turn (Relic of Legends versus Esika's granted ability)? Re-scope to one rules domain per scenario and resolve; neither may be cited until it passes.
Mikaeus, the Lunarch fetched rather than cast (does X=0 make him a 0/0?) needs a stack scenario — it decides whether the cold-start pool is three cards or two. The 99's pilot tip flags it as open.

Nine of the ten contained combo lines are unverified candidates (the Najeela variants, the Emiel blink loops, Ioreth–Samut–Selvala, the five-card Jegantha line). Only stack 002 is stated as fact anywhere in this issue.

The Short List opens four more stack-worthy lines (Walking Ballista + Heliod, Marvin + Ioreth, Staff of Domination + Selvala, Aggravated Assault + Selvala) — all flagged 'needs a stack scenario' in considering.json.

Strategy DB holes named in the strategic frame: toolbox/silver-bullet construction, access-as-a-resource, playing the stax seat proactively, removal-in-response as a gate attack, combat-loop finishers as a win-condition class, five-colour mana pricing, and restricted mana. All are research topics for the strategy-researcher.
